message.content:
**Traffic Laws in Texas – A Quick Overview** | Topic | Key Points | |-------|------------| | **Speed Limits** | • Posted limits apply unless otherwise specified.
• 55 mph on rural interstates, 65 mph on urban interstates, 45 mph on freeways, 35 mph on expressways.
• School zones: 25 mph (or 20 mph if posted). | | **Seat‑belt & Child Safety** | • All occupants must wear seat belts.
• Children under 8 must be in a child safety seat or booster. | | **Cell‑phone Use** | • Hand‑held devices are illegal while driving.
• Hands‑free devices are allowed. | | **Driving Under Influence (DUI)** | • Blood Alcohol Concentration (BAC) of 0.08% or higher is illegal.
• Zero‑tolerance for drivers under 21 (0.02% BAC). | | **Right‑of‑Way Rules** | • Yield to pedestrians at crosswalks.
• At uncontrolled intersections, vehicles on the right yield to those on the left. | | **School Bus** | • Stop on both sides when a school bus stops with its red lights flashing and stop sign extended. | | **Lane‑Changing & Overtaking** | • Must signal and check mirrors/blind spots.
• No “passing” on the right unless the vehicle ahead is turning left. | | **Parking Regulations** | • No parking within 20 ft of a fire hydrant.
• No parking on sidewalks unless permitted. | | **Traffic Signal Violations** | • Running a red light or stop sign is a moving violation. | | **Vehicle Equipment** | • Headlights must be on from sunset to sunrise.
• Tires must have adequate tread depth (2 / 32 in. minimum). | | **Insurance Requirements** | • Minimum liability coverage: $30,000 bodily injury per person, $60,000 total per accident, $25,000 property damage. | | **Towing & Tow‑away** | • Vehicles may be towed for violations such as illegal parking, abandoned vehicles, or if they pose a hazard. | ### How to Find Specific Statutes - **Texas Transportation Code** – Sections 545.001–545.999 cover most traffic laws. - **Texas Vehicle Code** – Sections 545.001–545.999 also include vehicle equipment and licensing requirements. - **Texas Department of Motor Vehicles (TxDMV)** – Offers downloadable handbooks and online resources. ### Common Enforcement Practices - Police use radar/lidar for speed enforcement. - DUI checkpoints are common, especially near major highways. - School bus enforcement is strict; violations can lead to fines and points on your license. ### Penalties - Moving violations typically result in points on your driver’s license, fines, and possible license suspension. - DUI convictions carry fines, mandatory alcohol education programs, and potential jail time. - Repeated offenses can lead to higher insurance rates and more severe penalties. --- #### Need More Detail? If you’re looking for a specific section of the Texas Transportation Code or want to know how a particular law applies to a situation (e.g., “What happens if I run a red light at a four‑way stop?”), let me know and I can pull up the exact statute or explain the legal implications.
